title: Phawar of Kinship Honor: Tip-Kur Tip-Kha
cultural_context: The central pillars of Khasi social law: honoring the maternal clan (*Kur*) and revering the father's relatives (*Kha*), set to rhyming phawar by Radhon Singh Berry.

khasi: Ba pynieng ia ka jaidbynriew baroh;
Ki kur ki dei ka snam ka doh,
Ki kha ki dei ka burom ba ai bor;
Burom ia u kñi uba hikai,
Khein kor ia ka bakha ba ieit;
Uba klet ia la ka kur bad ka kha
U long kum u dieng ba khlem thied.
english: Knowing maternal clan and paternal kin is the foundation,
That sustains and upholds our entire nation;
The maternal kur are our own flesh and blood,
The paternal kha are the honor that imparts strength;
Venerate the maternal uncle who instructs with wisdom,
Cherish with sacred regard the father's kindred;
He who turns his back on maternal and paternal kin
Is like a tree stripped of its living roots.

khasi: Wat pynkhein ia ka niam ka rukom,
Wat ialeh sang hakhmat U Blei;
Ka hok jong u Hynniewtrep ka neh,
Haba ngi tip ia la ka jait;
To ngin bat skhem ia kane ka akor,
Ha man ki tnum jong ka ri Khasi;
Ba ka burom jong ngi kan sah
english: Never violate our sacred ancestral customs,
Commit no clan taboo before Almighty God;
The righteousness of the Seven Huts endures,
When we know our lineage and clan bounds;
Let us hold fast to this noble heritage,
Beneath every thatched roof of the Khasi realm;
So that our ancestral honor may remain
From this day onward throughout all eternity.

vocabulary.kur: maternal clan members sharing common ancestress
